title: Recertification playbook: CI-driven validation + SIEM export + evidence checklist
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a lightweight operational playbook for quarterly least-privilege recertification that focuses on three practical goals: 1) fast, reproducible evidence generation via CI jobs; 2) a compact SIEM export payload/field mapping for auditors; and 3) minimal human workflow friction for reviewers (reminders, quick-approve flows, exception capture). It covers RBAC v2 mapping exports, sample audit-log schema to include, and the evidence bundle layout we expect to upload to GRC.

Why this doc exists (context)
- We need a repeatable, low-touch recertification run that produces convincing evidence for internal and external auditors.
- Previous cycles were too manual (screenshots, ad-hoc queries) and auditors asked for raw artifacts (policy snapshots + query output).
- This playbook is deliberately pragmatic: deliver a reproducible CI artifact and a SIEM-friendly summary that proves who had what access, who approved exceptions, and what activity was observed during the quarter.

High-level flow (quarterly)
1) Pre-run exports (T-7d): RBAC v2 snapshot, policy->role mapping, active members list, delegated owners list.
2) Automation run (T-3d): CI job queries audit logs, builds evidence bundle, runs validation tests (see "CI validation tests"), pushes bundle to S3 and creates GRC ticket.
3) Reviewer round (T+0..T+7d): reviewers receive email+Slack notifications, can use quick-approve link (one-click if no exceptions) or open exception form.
4) Audit packaging (T+8..T+14d): finalize bundle, sign-off, archive, and export SIEM snapshot for auditors.

Minimal evidence bundle (what auditors want)
- metadata.json (generated by CI) – includes run id, commit sha, run time, data ranges, exported-by service account id.
- rbac_snapshot.csv – flattened RBAC v2 mapping (role_id, role_name, permission_list, resource_selector, last_modified)
- memberships.csv – user/service-account -> role assignments with assignment_type and owner field
- exceptions.csv – any outstanding exceptions: requestor, approver, justification, expiry_date, ticket_id
- audit_sample.ndjson – raw audit events for the quarter filtered by critical actions (see schema below)
- validation.log – CI test results (checksums, record counts, sample queries)

RBAC v2 export recommendations (flattening rules)
- Expand composite roles into explicit permission lists in rbac_snapshot.csv. Don’t reference pointers to other objects; embed the resolved permissions to make the evidence self-contained.
- Include resource selectors as human-readable strings (e.g., "project:billing,env:prod"), and include the canonical resource IDs used by the runtime.
- For inherited permissions, include an inheritance_path column listing the chain.

Sample RBAC CSV header (order matters for audit reviewers):
role_id,role_name,permission_ids,permission_names,resource_selector,inheritance_path,last_modified

Audit log schema (NDJSON lines, one JSON per line) — minimal fields to include
Note: keep the schema compact but sufficient for forensic queries and SIEM correlation. The CI extracts a filtered subset and also pushes full raw exports to secure S3 for deep-dive.
- event_id: string (uuid)
- timestamp: ISO-8601
- actor: { type: user|service_account, id: string }  -- serialized as actor_type and actor_id in flattened NDJSON for SIEM compatibility
- action: string (e.g., role.assign, role.revoke, policy.update, session.start, session.end, token.create)
- target: string (resource canonical id)
- target_type: string (role|policy|instance|dataset)
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- request_id: string
- source_ip: string
- reason: string (free text, may be empty)
- auth_context: e.g., mfa=true, location=us-east1 (flattened as key=value; semicolon separated)
- trace_id: string

Example NDJSON line we generate from the CI job (flattened for the SIEM):
{"event_id":"f2d0a9c8-7e1a-4a2c-b3b9-8d1b3d2f7c3a","timestamp":"2025-09-11T14:22:03Z","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"a.patel@redwood.com","action":"role.assign","target":"role:dedicated-admin","target_type":"role","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-98765","source_ip":"18.205.12.45","reason":"onboarding:dedicated-team","auth_context":"mfa=true;location=us-west-1","trace_id":"trace-44f2"}

CI validation tests (run as part of recert job)
- Count sanity: rbac_snapshot.csv rows == expected_role_count (fail if missing >1%)
- Membership cross-check: every membership in memberships.csv must reference an existing role_id in rbac_snapshot.csv
- Exceptions TTL: exceptions.csv entries without expiry_date older than 90 days -> fail the job and create a follow-up ticket
- Sample event correlation: audit_sample.ndjson should contain at least one role.assign/event for each role modified during the quarter (smoke check)
- Signature check: uploaded bundle has GPG signature (or internal KMS envelope) attached

SIEM export mapping (compact summary for auditors)
- We push two things to SIEM: 1) the filtered NDJSON lines (critical actions), and 2) a one-line per-role summary event for quick pivoting. This summary event has lower cardinality and helps auditors rapidly scan the dataset.
- summary_event fields: run_id, role_id, total_assigns, total_revokes, active_members_count, exceptions_count, last_modified

Sample summary event (JSON line):
{"run_id":"recert-2025Q4-1123","role_id":"role:dedicated-admin","total_assigns":12,"total_revokes":3,"active_members_count":8,"exceptions_count":1,"last_modified":"2025-10-19T03:12:00Z"}

Reviewer UX and quick-approve flow
- By default we send a consolidated email and Slack DM with three items: 1) link to bundle in S3 (signed URL), 2) quick-approve link, 3) link to open exception form.
- Quick-approve: clicking the link records reviewer id, timestamp and uses the reviewer’s id token to write an approval record to approvals.csv in the bundle. If any reviewer opens the exception form, the run is flagged for human follow-up.
- If a reviewer does not respond in 5 business days, automated nudges fire (day 3 and day 5). After day 7 a manual escalator ticket is created for the manager.

Exception capture and minimal required evidence for approvals
- Any exception requires: justification, approving manager (with manager_id), explicit expiry (max 90 days), and a linked ticket id. The exceptions.csv entry must include these fields exactly; otherwise the CI fails the packaging step.

For auditors: what we commit to deliver
- A reproducible S3 bundle with metadata.json + rbac_snapshot.csv + memberships.csv + exceptions.csv + audit_sample.ndjson + validation.log.
- SIEM snapshot with compact mapping + filtered NDJSON for critical events. We will also hand over the CI job id and commit sha so auditors can re-run the CI in read-only mode to regenerate the same bundle.

Operational notes and TODOs (team action items)
- [ ] Add "resolve-composite-roles" step to the RBAC export script (owner: Tomas)
- [ ] Update CI to attach KMS envelope instead of GPG (security review pending; owner: Maya)
- [ ] Add more actionable summary fields to the summary_event (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Create a Confluence quick-runner doc for reviewers with sample language for exception justifications (owner: Ethan)

References and quick links
- Confluence: SEC-RECERT-2025 (master policy and background)
- Jira: SEC-4319 (recert automation epic)
- GH: redwood-infra/recertification-automation (CI job + exporters)
- Slack: #sec-recert for run day troubleshooting

Notes to auditors / FAQ (short)
Q: Can we provide raw logs?
A: Yes — raw quarterly audit exports are archived to protected S3; we provide a signed temporary link on request and include a checksum in metadata.json.

Q: What if a reviewer claims they did not receive the quick-approve link?
A: All notifications include the run_id and a fallback link to the bundle; we also log email/DM delivery status. If delivery fails we escalate automatically.

Q: Are service accounts included?
A: Yes. memberships.csv explicitly lists actor_type for each assignment (user|service_account) and the CI includes service account activity in audit_sample.ndjson.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets
- Export RBAC snapshot (one-off): ./scripts/export_rbac_v2.sh --out rbac_snapshot.csv --resolve-composite
- Run CI extraction locally: ./ci/run_recert_job.sh --start 2025-10-01 --end 2025-12-31 --dry-run
- Validate bundle: ./tools/validate_recert_bundle.py bundle-dir/

End of playbook (working draft)

Notes: keep feedback in this doc for now; we will fold the stable steps into Confluence and mark the CI-run artifacts / tests as the canonical evidence.
